summary: Frontend-only regression for multi-image support, product reorder, and JK Velvet cover images. All acceptance criteria pass. Products page default order matches spec (brasso-velvet, micro-11000-falcon, micro-9000-velvet, micro-velvet-99999, viscose-velvet, coco-velvet, ...). Category filter buttons render 'Weaving Velvet (5)', 'Flocked Velvet (9)', 'Raising Velvet (6)' and filter correctly (knitting -> twilight, holland-velvet, kabul-velvet, lycra-velvet, mosha-velvet, raising-velvet). Every product has 2 images (cover + context fallback). Product detail viewer shows one large image with a thumbnail strip (grid, no arrows), unique data-testids per thumbnail. Clicking Brasso thumb 2 swaps main image to /assets/general/denim-stack.webp and counter to 01/02 -> 02/02. Route change to /products/coco-velvet correctly resets to coverIndex (01/02, coco-velvet-cover.webp). All 20 /assets/products/*-cover.webp files exist locally and load. Category cards + gallery tiles + related products use new cover images. Mobile viewport (390px) shows thumbnails in a 2-col grid with no horizontal overflow. No console errors observed.
critical_code_review_comments: productImages() dedupes by URL and always appends the context image from IMAGES[p.img]. This is why every product currently gets 2 images even though products.js lists only one entry in `images`. Works as intended per user spec but the data model is a bit implicit—consider explicitly listing both images in products.js so `images` is truly the source of truth.

ProductDetail thumbnail strip uses `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4` — fine for 2 images, but if more images are added later, portrait mobile will jump to a very tight 2-col layout. Consider a horizontal scroll strip for >4 images.
coverIndex resets on slug change via useEffect, but if the same product's coverIndex updates without slug change (e.g., admin edit) the dependency `product?.coverIndex` covers it — good.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend static SPA. Cover images at /assets/products/<slug>-cover.webp. productImages() in catalog.js dedupes cover + IMAGES[p.img]; if a product ever has images identical to its context IMAGES entry, only 1 thumbnail will render and the thumb strip is hidden by design (images.length > 1 guard).
